followup_explanation:
This is a creative generation task (drafting a personal statement response) with a tight constraint (300 characters, concise). Here's my reasoning:

- **Capability:** Dunlin leads on the relevant internal evals — Creative Generation 84.7 vs 82.7 (a tie, under 2.0) but it's also stronger on IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3) and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2), which matter here since the user wants precise instruction-following: a hard character cap and "don't ramble."

- **Task preferences:** Willet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, and this task has real latitude (composing a motivational statement). While that aversion is dissociated from quality, there's no upside to routing toward a model that disprefers the work when the other model handles it at least as well and follows instructions more reliably.

The instruction-adherence edge (character limit + concision) was the deciding factor.
